column4: A dead sharing sign-in now goes to the rejoin state and keeps its unsent rows instead of becoming a new anonymous user.
Signing out is refused while any change is set aside and editing the item clears its set-aside entry.
A collection's own row keeps only as much order as fits so it is never set aside and the member rows carry every recipe.
Leaving or deleting household data sends unsent rows first and refuses if they can't be sent.
Data saved by a newer build is never loaded as empty or saved over.
A plan saved with odd fields loads as empty fields so startup and sync still finish.
Other members' recipes the plan uses stay when sharing stops; marking plan rows that point at deleted recipes is server-side.
Every saved store is listed as cleared on sign-out or deletion or kept and deletion now clears the Home log.
A lapsed sign-in keeps its unsent rows sends them on signing back in and tells the person once.
The code error no longer promises single-use codes or a two-day life.
Cooking skill and intents now sync with the account.
Joining a household or signing in drops weeks past the 8-week keep.
Adopting a household is single-flight so two at once pull once.
The old-app import marks itself pending then done and a re-run uses the same ids so nothing doubles.
Invite previews no longer create an anonymous user on a fresh phone.
Startup waits for all 15 saved stores and a test checks the list against the source.
A household function missing on the server reads as not available instead of a vague failure.
Link import reads the page as a stream and stops at the 5 MB cap.
Imported ingredients and method are cut to fit a backed-up row and the notes say so.
Cupboard matching is worked out once per change and shared by every screen.
The account merge retry keeps one timer instead of stacking them.
Client half: Apple's code goes to apple-token and deletion calls delete-account with the RPC fallback; server half is the server fixer's.
